changes: Weights rounded to one decimal from the Wikipedia ranges: hen 2.15 to 2.2 kg (2.0 to 2.3 kg) and rooster 2.65 to 2.7 kg (2.5 to 2.8 kg). Varieties black, white, buff, cuckoo to black: those four colors are what Pochini illustrated in 1900, but the breed today is the black Valdarno (Wikipedia: an Italian breed of black chicken; the 1905 standard noted the black predominated). Added comb single (Wikipedia infobox). Dual purpose and Tuscan origin confirmed by FAO DAD-IS (eggs and meat, both very good). White eggs, skin, earlobes, conservation status and history match Wikipedia. Weights rest on one publisher, so needs_review stays true.

summary.value: The Valdarno is a black dual purpose chicken from the lower Arno valley in Tuscany, in the farm country between Florence, Pisa and the sea. It should not be confused with the Valdarnese, a white breed from the upper valley. Writers praised it around 1900 for fast growth and good mothering, and a standard was set in 1905, when a local saying held that only a black chicken was a real one. Competition from the White Leghorn later pushed it almost to extinction. Breeders rebuilt it from a few birds found near Siena, crossed with Bresse and Castellana Negra, and showed the results in 1998. The bird is black with a green sheen, slate legs, white skin, a red single comb and white earlobes. Roosters weigh about 5.5 to 6.2 pounds and hens 4.4 to 5 pounds. Hens lay white eggs. Only about 200 breeding birds were counted in 2007.
